name: Whiskey Rapids Trail
why: Looped Highway 60 trail to Whiskey Rapids on the Oxtongue River.

name: Hardwood Lookout Trail
why: Short Highway 60 trail to a Smoke Lake lookout; page does not say loop or one way.

name: Mizzy Lake Trail
why: Full-day Highway 60 trail past nine ponds; page does not say loop or one way.

name: Peck Lake Trail
why: Trail around Peck Lake, so it is a loop.

name: Track and Tower Trail
why: Looped trail with a Cache Lake lookout; the optional 5.5 km side trip is not included.

name: Hemlock Bluff Trail
why: Highway 60 trail to a view of Jack Lake; page does not say loop or one way.

name: Bat Lake Trail
why: Looped Highway 60 trail past a lookout and Bat Lake.

name: Two Rivers Trail
why: Short looped trail up to a pine-clad cliff.

name: Centennial Ridges Trail
why: Demanding loop along two high ridges.

name: Big Pines Trail
why: Trail through old-growth white pine; page does not say loop or one way.

name: Booth's Rock Trail
why: Goes out past two lakes and a lookout and returns another way (old railway), so it is a loop.

name: Spruce Bog Boardwalk
why: Looped boardwalk trail through two spruce bogs.

name: Fork Lake Trail
why: Steep short trail from the Visitor Centre; page does not say loop or one way.

name: Algonquin Logging Museum Trail
why: Trail through the logging museum exhibits; page does not say loop or one way.

name: Lookout Trail
why: Steep short trail to a big lookout; page does not say loop or one way.

name: Beaver Pond Trail
why: Trail with views of two beaver ponds; page does not say loop or one way.

name: Highland Backpacking Trail
why: Named backpacking trail; the longer 35 km loop is used (a 19 km loop also exists).

name: Western Uplands Backpacking Trail
why: Named backpacking trail; the longest 88 km loop is used (three loops, 32 to 88 km).

name: Eastern Pines Backpacking Trail
why: Named backpacking trail; the longest 15 km loop is used (loops of 6 to 15 km).

name: High Falls Hiking Trail
why: Southern section: from the High Falls parking area to the falls.

name: Barron Canyon Trail
why: Eastern section, off the Sand Lake Gate road: a short loop to the rim of the Barron Canyon.

name: Berm Lake Trail
why: Eastern section: around Berm Lake from the Achray Campground.

name: Jack Pine Trail
why: Eastern section, near Achray: a short walk through jack pine forest.

name: Brent Crater Trail
why: Northern section, off Brent Road: down into a meteorite crater and back to the start.
